D011-D020_h001.question: It all started about two months ago when my bank branch was acquired. I've been a manager for years, and suddenly, everything felt uncertain. Since then, I’ve just been a wreck. I wake up every morning with this knot in my stomach, and it’s just constant worry, every single day. I find myself fixating on all the what-ifs, the new management, potential layoffs, all of it. I try to tell myself to stop, to just breathe, but it’s like my brain won’t let go. My nerves are completely shot; the slightest unexpected noise, like a phone ringing too loudly, makes me jump out of my skin. And my body feels it too. My muscles ache practically everywhere – my back, my shoulders, my legs, just a constant, dull pain that never seems to ease up. It all just started after the acquisition, and it’s made everything so much harder. I just can't seem to relax.
D011-D020_h001.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D011-D020_h002.question: "Honestly, I've just been a mess since the news about the department restructuring came out a little over two months ago. It sounds silly, but I can't shake this feeling that if I mess up even a tiny bit, I'm going to be first on the chopping block, and then what? My whole career goes down the drain. This worry just barges into my head, even when I'm trying to crunch numbers or write reports, making it impossible to focus. I'm constantly on edge, jumping at every little sound in the office, like a phone vibrating or someone clearing their throat. My neck and shoulders feel like solid knots, practically cemented, and I've got this constant dull headache. It's really impacting my work and my sleep. Before this whole restructuring debacle, I felt fine, just typical work stress, but nothing like this constant dread."
D011-D020_h002.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D011-D020_h003.question:
It all started a few months ago, right after they restructured the newsroom and brought in a new lead anchor. I know it sounds silly, but suddenly, every little "what if" about my career has amplified into a deafening roar. I’m constantly asking myself, "What if I get sidelined? What if my ratings drop? What if I lose my spot?" I try to push these thoughts away, tell myself to focus, but they just loop in my head.

Honestly, it feels like I'm wound up so tight that I could snap. I can’t relax, even at home. My neck and shoulders are practically fused together; it's a constant ache that sometimes turns into a pounding headache. It’s been happening for about two months now, and while this new work situation is still ongoing, I worry about it getting worse, not better, if I can’t get a handle on it.
D011-D020_h003.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D011-D020_h004.question: Lately, it just feels like I’m running on fumes, Doc. Since the shop I’ve worked at for fifteen years announced it’s closing down, I can’t stop my mind from racing. It’s been about two months now, and I’m constantly asking myself, "What if I don't find another job? What if I can't provide for my family?" These thoughts just pop into my head out of nowhere, even when I'm trying to fix something, and then I lose my place. I feel this constant tension, like I’m wound up tight, and I can't really relax. My shoulders and back are always stiff and aching, and my legs feel tired, almost like I've run a marathon, even when I haven’t. It all started right after the news about the shop. Before that, I was fine. Now, I’m just waiting for the other shoe to drop.
D011-D020_h004.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D011-D020_h005.question: It’s been almost five months now since my mother passed, and I just can't seem to get a handle on things. The worrying never stops. It’s like one little thought can set off a whole chain reaction in my head - I’ll start fretting about the library budget, then suddenly I'm convinced I'll lose my job, then I'll be homeless, and then… well, it just spirals. I feel keyed up all the time, like I’m wound too tight. My muscles ache constantly, especially in my back and shoulders, and I'm always tired even when I’ve done nothing. Before August, when my mother got sick, I never felt this way. I mean, everyone worries, but this constant, pervasive anxiety really only kicked in after we got her diagnosis and things became so stressful. It just feels different now.
D011-D020_h005.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D011-D020_h006.question: "Well, doctor, it all started a couple of months ago, right after my retirement party. You'd think I'd be relieved, you know? But ever since I stopped going into the office, I just… I can't settle. I'm wound up like a spring, can't sit still for a minute, even when I'm just trying to read the paper. My wife says I'm pacing the floors. And the worrying! It’s not just one thing, it’s everything. I worry about our pension, about the house, about my son getting that promotion at his job, even about the weather forecast for next week. It's like my mind just jumps from one worry to the next, no rhyme or reason to it. And I’m sleeping more than ever. I'll sleep a solid ten hours at night, and still feel like I need a nap in the afternoon. It’s not like me at all. It really has got worse since I retired."
D011-D020_h006.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D011-D020_h007.question: It’s tough to pinpoint exactly when things started feeling this way, but after the accident at the plant a few months back – the one where Kevin lost his arm – everything just changed. I can’t stop replaying it, even though I wasn’t directly involved in the incident itself. I remember it was within three months of that happening, maybe two, that the sleep really went downhill. I just lie there, tossing and turning, my mind racing about the smallest things at work. I keep thinking, "What if that happens to one of my guys, and it’s my fault?" Even a tiny error on a report, I'm convinced it's going to lead to some massive, irreversible disaster that will get me fired or worse. And I'm on edge all the time. My wife will just walk into the room, or the phone will ring, and I’ll jump out of my skin. It's been like this ever since that accident, and it’s still lingering, even though the official investigations are over. Honestly, I never really felt this stressed about work before then.
D011-D020_h007.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D011-D020_h008.question:

I can't shake the feeling that one little hiccup, one misplaced ingredient, and it's all over.

I’m exhausted all the time. I'll sleep for eight hours, but I wake up feeling like I haven't slept a wink. My muscles are constantly tight, especially in my shoulders. It's like my body is ready for a fight, but there's nothing to fight. This level of worry, it's new for me, and it really kicked in after that inspection. Before that, I handled stress just fine. D011-D020_h012.question: Lately, I’ve just been running on fumes, completely drained. It all started a few weeks after the accident on site – you know, when the boom buckled.     B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D011-D020_h013.question:

A. Bipolar I Disorder

D011-D020_h015.question: Doctor, I'm just… I'm not myself lately. It all started after the break-in at the warehouse, about two months ago.
